questions.q: By default, is a Batch Apex job's instance variable value reliably preserved from one chunk's execute call to the next?
options: Yes — all instance variables always persist across every chunk automatically
Only static variables persist by default; instance variables never do, even with Database.Stateful
No — Batch Apex is stateless by default, so instance variables aren't guaranteed to carry their value between chunk transactions
It depends on the batch chunk size specified in Database.executeBatch
questions.explain: Batch Apex is stateless by default — each chunk's execute call is a separate transaction, and instance variables aren't reliably preserved between them unless the class implements Database.Stateful.

questions.q: What does adding Database.Stateful to a batch class's declaration do?
options: It increases the default chunk size from 200 to 2,000
It allows the batch job to make HTTP callouts
It forces every chunk to run in a single shared transaction instead of separate ones
It preserves instance member variables' values across all of the job's chunk transactions
questions.explain: Database.Stateful is a marker interface that tells the platform to preserve instance member variables' values across every transaction in the batch job, instead of resetting them each chunk.

questions.q: A batch class declares 'public static Integer counter = 0;' instead of an instance variable, and implements Database.Stateful. What's the problem?
options: There is no problem; static and instance variables behave identically under Database.Stateful
Database.Stateful preserves instance member variables, not static variables — a static field isn't what this interface is meant to preserve
Static variables cannot be declared in a Batch Apex class at all
Database.Stateful only works with String fields, never Integer fields
questions.explain: Database.Stateful specifically preserves instance member variables across transactions. A static variable follows its own separate rules and shouldn't be relied on to carry state between chunks this way.

questions.q: Which scenario is a good concrete reason to add Database.Stateful to a batch class?
options: Updating each record in scope based only on fields already present on that same record, with no shared total needed
Database.Stateful is required on every Batch Apex class regardless of use case
Accumulating a running count of records processed, to report an accurate total in finish
Avoiding the default chunk size of 200 records
questions.explain: Database.Stateful is specifically useful when a value — like a running total of records processed, or an accumulating list of failures — needs to survive from one chunk to the next so finish can report it accurately.

questions.q: If every chunk's work in a batch job is fully independent, with no running total or shared counter needed, what's the recommended default?
options: Always add Database.Stateful anyway, just in case requirements change later
Switch to Queueable Apex instead, since Batch Apex cannot run without Database.Stateful
Use a static variable instead of Database.Stateful for better performance
Leave the class stateless — Database.Stateful adds complexity with no actual benefit in that case
questions.explain: When no value genuinely needs to persist across chunks, a stateless batch is simpler and has nothing extra to reason about — Database.Stateful should be reserved for jobs that actually need to carry a value between transactions.
